title: Fast-cut Feature Trimmer — notes
content:
Context:
I keep running into the same problem during capacity reviews: a long tail of low-usage features and flags that add complexity to serving (extra model variants, routing rules, added latency). We need a leaner path to surgically remove or dark-launch feature behavior that is materially hurting inference economics, while preserving safety and product continuity.

High-level idea (the mower analogy):
- Treat feature surface like a lawn: identify overgrown/weedy spots (features consuming disproportionate tokens or causing routing churn) and trim them quickly, not full redesigns.
- Provide a small operator toolkit (UI + API + audit trail) to queue, preview, and roll back quick trims.

Hypothesis:
- Removing or consolidating the worst 5% of feature/flag cases will reduce total per-token cost by ~3–6% for affected tenants and reduce median latency by ~8–12% for routed requests (less variant switching).

Goals / success metrics (first 90 days):
- Launch an internal PoC: "trim queue" + CLI to stage trims for 10 pilot routes.
- Metric: per-route median latency improvement >= 5% for at least 6 of 10 pilots.
- Metric: end-to-end token spend reduction >= 2% across pilots.
- Safety: zero customer-facing regressions (monitored via eval prompt sets and user telemetry).

User stories (rough):
- As an Ops engineer, I want to queue a candidate trim (description + affected routes + rollback plan) so I can batch low-risk removals for review.
- As a PM, I want to preview projected cost/latency gains and the list of example requests affected so I can sign off.
- As an SRE, I want automatic smoke checks (sampled traffic test) and a canary rollout that can be auto-rolled back on error.
- As a data analyst, I want exported diffs (before/after request samples, token counts) so I can validate real impact.

Proposed primitives / components:
- Trim candidate model: small JSON describing the change: feature id, variant mapping (old->fallback), reason, risk level, owner, expected delta (est cost/latency), linked eval set.
- Trim queue: CRUD + comments + approvals (simple lightweight UI in Console).
- Preview mode: run sampled traffic with feature masked/redirected to fallback in a sandbox (no real user impact) and produce report.
- Canary runner: deploy to a configurable percent of traffic with rollback hooks and automated triggers (error count, delta QoQ regression on eval prompts).
- Audit/logging: immutable audit records + human notes on reasoning.

Experiment plan:
- Phase 0: data sweep (1 week) — identify candidate features across hosted tenants by: token per-feature, variant switch rate, route churn, and QoR (e.g., hallucination or failure increase).
- Phase 1: offline sandbox preview (2 weeks) — run sampled replay for top 20 candidates, produce delta reports.
- Phase 2: internal pilots (4 weeks) — 10 internal customers or low-risk tenants at 1% then 10% rollout with automated rollback.
- Phase 3: evaluate and decide: revert, merge to standard routing policy, or codify as permanent removal.

Acceptance criteria for a "trim" to go live:
- Preview sandbox shows no QoR regression on the linked eval set (threshold configurable, default 0.5% allowed regression).
- Token savings estimate validated by replay within +/- 20%.
- Owner + PM approval recorded in queue.
- Canary completes with no automated rollback triggers for 48 hours at 10% traffic.

Safety & rollback considerations:
- Always provide an explicit fallback mapping; never route to a new model variant without fallback.
- Default auto-rollback triggers: 5xx rate increase > 0.2%, token-per-request delta > 30% unexpectedly, eval prompt failure delta > threshold.
- Rolling time windows and backoff to avoid thrashing.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- What is the canonical identifier for a "feature"? (flag key vs. behavior fingerprint vs. prompt module) — choose lowest friction while still specific.
- How to handle tenant-owned customizations (feature present for some tenants but not others)? Probably per-tenant trim records and visibility scoping.
- Can we automate candidate scoring with an estimator (cost delta + risk) to surface highest ROI trims? If so, what features feed into it?
- Is a UI necessary initially or will an API + spreadsheet vetting be faster? MVP: API + CLI + prebuilt spreadsheet export.

Implementation quick sketch (MVP):
- Back-end: "trim-service" small microservice that stores candidates, runs sandbox replays (uses existing request-replay infra), triggers canaries via existing rollout APIs.
- Console: minimal "trim queue" page (table + preview link + approve button). Could be a scoped Console workbench tab.
- Metrics: reuse tracing & cost telemetry; add per-trim tags to correlate metrics.

Edge cases to document:
- Feature that changes request shaping (shorter prompts) — trimming may improve cost but degrade quality in corner cases.
- Feature gating tied to compliance (cannot auto-trim without legal signoff).
- Interactions with caching/batching: trimming could change cache hit patterns—measure.

Rollout notes + quick TODOs:
- [ ] Run data sweep query: top 100 low-usage flags by token cost (owner: Mira) — due 2025-01-24
- [ ] Wire up replay pipeline for preview mode (owner: Ethan) — due 2025-02-05
- [ ] Sketch Console wireframe (owner: me) — due 2025-01-30
- [ ] Draft approval rubric and rollback thresholds (owner: Priya) — due 2025-02-01
- [ ] Sync with legal on compliance-scoped features (owner: Hector) — due 2025-02-07

Quick notes to self (brain-dump):
- Keep initial UX minimal: triage list + two-button preview/approve instead of full ticketing workflow.
- If we can show 2% cost reduction across some tenants quickly, that'll be a compelling narrative for Dedicated customers to request a "feature hygiene" audit.
- Label everything "reversible" in audit logs to reduce fear.

References / inspiration:
- internal: token-batching-hierarchy-journal (revisit for batching interactions)
- external: paper on feature toggles and technical debt (link to saved PDF)

Next meeting agenda (sync with Mira/Ethan/Priya):
- share data sweep results
- finalize MVP scope (API + replay + canary)
- ownership & milestones for the 6-week pilot

End of note.
